key_insight: VecTile uses passive silicone nubs to convert normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns, enabling low-cost three-axis tactile sensing.
engineering_relevance: The flexible, 6 mm-thin array provides robots with contact-force feedback for grasp stability and manipulation at under $35 for a 4×4 array.
method: Combine a piezoresistive sensing layer with passive silicone nubs.
Validate force-to-pressure conversion using finite element analysis and hardware experiments.
Calibrate force estimates and test curved operation and robotic applications.
evidence_signal: Controlled single-taxel tests spanning 1–5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force achieved RMSEs of 0.39 N for normal force and 0.16 N for shear force.
watch_item: Reported force errors come from controlled single-taxel tests; they do not establish full-array accuracy under simultaneous, complex contacts.
paper_title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
